sections.overview: The Common Gull breeds widely across the northern Palearctic. It shares genus Larus with the Lesser Black-backed Gull and Glaucous Gull covered alongside it here.
sections.identification: Adults have a grey back and greenish-yellow bill and legs.
sections.habitat: It nests on coasts and inland, including moorland, lake shores and river banks.
sections.diet: Inland birds take worms and insects; coastal birds also eat crustaceans, molluscs and small fish.
sections.behavior: It often breeds colonially, then gathers in groups outside the nesting season.
sections.reproduction: Nests are usually on the ground, though trees and artificial structures can also be used.
sections.ecology: Its varied prey links food webs in inland fields, freshwater edges and coastal waters.
sections.conservation: IUCN lists it as Least Concern globally. British monitoring places the breeding population on the UK Red List.
